Sokolka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sokółka, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Sokółka in the 17th century; by 1921, 2,821 Jews (46%) were mostly murdered by Germans 1942-1943. This cemetery traces to a formal 1698 privilege from King August II the Strong, granting the Jewish community permission to establish 'a mound to bury the dead.' A 1981 government survey noted the last burial occurred in 1945; a 1949 attempt by the Central Committee of Jews in Poland to trade cemetery upkeep for management of the former synagogue reflects postwar community efforts to preserve local heritage. A 1987 inventory by Tomasz Wiśniewski and Andrzej Grajter counted 1,067 surviving matzevot; an information board was added in 2007, and volunteer Ewa Krychniak has led periodic student cleanups for over a decade.
